and that no `ops-internal` key lands in the bucket registry. The old exemption test only pinned one route and one tier.
- `limiter/bucket.py:7` — docstring said "refills one token at a time over `refill_ms`", which misdescribes the parameter; `refill_ms` is the time to refill the whole burst. Corrected.

## Verification
`python3 -m pytest -q` → **16 passed** (was 15). The new test also passes standalone, and I re-ran the full suite to confirm it is not order-dependent — the first version was (`assert _BUCKETS == {}` failed once other tests ran), so it now asserts only that no exempt-tenant key exists.

One thing worth flagging: if the rule you had in mind isn't the exemption, the only genuinely undetermined point in this spec is gold refill granularity — "one token every 1500/37 ms" versus "refill time stays 1500 ms" contradict each other under 2× burst. I implemented the second reading (per-token interval 1500/74 ms, full refill still 1500 ms), which is the only self-consistent one. Say the word if you want the other.
